content.comment_body: I'm relatively new to working with [company_name] [product_name] without display and could use some guidance. I've received several files on a memory stick, and at least one is required to make the equipment work properly. However, I'm unsure whether I need just one or all of them. The files are named: Circuit Diagram1.lsc, Project.mnp, XXX.lsc, XXXX-Copy.lsc, and XXXX_v81.lsc. I've transferred all these files to an SD card and inserted it into the PLC, but it doesn't start, and the LED stays red. Am I causing confusion by loading too many programs? The setup is standalone, with just a single PLC and an expansion module, and is not networked. Any advice would be appreciated.

Only one program is able to run in the [product_name]. When transferring your desired program from among your five files to the SD card, ensure it is saved in the correct format. First, open the required program file and verify that the hardware settings match your device. Then use 'Save as' to save the program as a binary dump (*.bin), which will automatically suggest the correct file name, such as 'LOGO_U_P'. Copy this file onto the SD card, which should be formatted to FAT32 and have a maximum size of no more than 32 GB.

analysis.insight_summary: The user has difficulty transferring program files to a [product_name] without display, causing the device to remain in error mode (red LED). There is uncertainty about which file format to use and limitations regarding file quantity. The replies clarify that only a single, correctly named and formatted binary file is supported, exposing a gap in user guidance and automation for those less experienced with this hardware.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes for an easy and automatic file transfer process with the [product_name], expecting the equipment to recognize the correct program and operate without requiring advanced understanding of file formats or manual selection.
